llm.summary: This skill is a bounded soccer match analysis helper that uses a documented Crawlora/SofaScore API workflow and does not show hidden persistence, privilege escalation, or unrelated data access.

dimensions.detail: Network access to https://api.crawlora.net/api/v1 and a CRAWLORA_API_KEY are required; the helper fixes the base URL, restricts routes to the documented SofaScore endpoints, uses GET only, and URL-encodes query parameters.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The package ships an executable shell helper but no auto-install or auto-run behavior was found; tool permissions are not declared, so users should expect shell and network use when the helper is invoked.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The instructions limit default work to one match, require event verification, preserve live/upcoming status, ask before broad collection, and explicitly avoid unsupported tactical or causal claims.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No persistent services, hooks, memory writes, or privilege escalation were found; the helper creates a temporary curl config for the API key with restrictive permissions and removes it on exit.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The stated purpose is to produce source-grounded post-match soccer reports from SofaScore event data, and the artifacts support that with search, event detail, statistics, incidents, lineups, optional h2h/team-events, and optional odds endpoints.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Before installing, understand that using this skill sends match search terms, event IDs, and your Crawlora API key to Crawlora's API. This is expected for the workflow, but users who do not want a third-party sports-data proxy or who cannot share those queries should avoid using it.
llm.findings:
[LP3] expected: The shell examples are real execution guidance, but the script itself is narrowly scoped to GET-only documented routes and rejects alternate methods and unrelated paths; the missing explicit permission metadata is a packaging note rather than a material security concern here.
[E1] expected: External transmission to api.crawlora.net is disclosed and necessary for the skill's data retrieval purpose; the sent data appears limited to the Crawlora API key header and match/search query parameters for the documented endpoints.
[PE2] expected: The flagged chmod 600 command does not invoke sudo or root privileges; it restricts permissions on a temporary curl config file holding the API key and is removed via trap on exit.
